subject: Grace period & one-time smoothing credit for initial commit — proposal and next steps

Date: Sun, 21 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Grace period & one-time smoothing credit for initial commit — proposal and next steps

Hi Lisa —

Thanks again for the productive call yesterday. As promised, attached is a short proposal from our side that aims to address Orchard’s concern about early-stage variability in usage while keeping contract economics aligned for both parties. High level:

- One-time smoothing credit applied to the first billing quarter (applies only to overage true-ups above the committed band)
- 60-day grace window before any mid-year upward adjustment is applied
- A reconciliation / clawback if annualized run-rate falls below 70% of the committed volume by the end of Q4

We’ve attached a redlined pricing schedule (Proposed Pricing Schedule - ORCH v2.pdf) and a short annotated spreadsheet showing examples. Two asks from you: (1) confirm whether a 60-day grace window is acceptable as a concept, and (2) share any legal redline language your counsel will need so we can produce a DocuSign-ready amendment.

If it helps, I can loop in our finance partner Soojin for a quick math walk-through — she’s cc’d. If you’re available, I’d like to get this onto a short review next week so we can close this quarter.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz

Date: Mon, 22 Sep 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Grace period & one-time smoothing credit for initial commit — proposal and next steps

Vanessa —

Thanks for the note and attachments. I ran the material by our procurement/legal leads and they appreciate the intent, but they asked for two changes before we can accept in principle:

1) Narrow the clawback language — they want a capped clawback (no more than 25% of the smoothing credit) rather than a full revenue reversal.
2) Replace the 60-day grace window with a defined "onboarding ramp" period tied to activation milestones (first 90 days or first 10k active monthly users, whichever occurs first).

I’ve attached our redline (Orchard-redline-pricing-clause.pdf) with comments. They also asked to see a final pricing schedule as clean text (not embedded in a long amendment) so it’s easier to pull into our procurement system.

If we can get a revised clause that caps the clawback and ties the timing to onboarding milestones, procurement is comfortable moving to signatures quickly.

Appreciate you looping finance in — I think a short alignment call with legal on both sides would clear the remaining items.

—Lisa
Lisa Turner
Head of Strategic Partnerships | Orchard HealthTech

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Sep 2025 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Grace period & one-time smoothing credit for initial commit — proposal and next steps

Vanessa / Soojin —

Reading through Orchard’s redline. High-level internal take: we can agree to cap the clawback at 25% of the smoothing credit (makes sense commercially). However, tying the timing to a milestone that includes MAUs introduces measurement and audit complexity on our side. Proposal:

- Accept capped clawback (25% max of smoothing credit)
- Keep time-based grace window but increase to 90 days (aligns with onboarding ramp)
- Add a short audit clause that lets Orchard request usage detail for the first 6 months (with mutual confidentiality) to verify ramp metrics; limit requests to one reconciliation event per year to avoid operational burden

Soojin — can you run the numbers on expected cash impact for a 90-day vs 60-day window and confirm if the cap looks acceptable from a revenue ops perspective? If it’s smallish, I’ll draft a short clause for legal to insert into the pricing schedule.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0124

Lisa —

Thanks — that read is helpful and I think Karthik’s compromises are reasonable. Per our internal check:

- We accept capped clawback at 25% of the smoothing credit.
- We’ll move the grace window to 90 days and state it as an "initial onboarding period (90 days)" to align with Orchard’s ask.
- We’ll include a single reconciliation audit right for the first 6 months (limited scope and confidentiality obligations).

I’ve drafted the short clause and attached it as a one-page clean text insert (Proposed pricing clause text). If Orchard agrees to that language, we can prepare an amendment for signature. I’ll also include a clean pricing schedule CSV to make procurement ingestion easier.

Would you like me to generate the DocuSign envelope and send for signature pending your legal sign-off on the one-page clause? If so, I’ll send the link and proposed signer list.
